title: Finite-type approximation of an affine nodal family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the geometric fibre $X_\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and every point where $X_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $x\in X$ be a point at which $f$ is not smooth and set $s=f(x)$. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $X^\circ\subseteq X$ of $x$ and $S^\circ\subseteq S$ of $s$, with $f(X^\circ)\subseteq S^\circ$, schemes $X_0,S_0$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a flat finitely presented morphism $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, and a Cartesian square $X^\circ\cong X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$ [def-pc-fibre-product] over a morphism $S^\circ\to S_0$. The morphism $f_0$ has the same geometric-fibre condition: every nonempty geometric fibre is pure of dimension $1$ and its completed local ring at every nonsmooth point is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The image $x_0\in X_0$ of $x$ is nonsmooth for $f_0$. Here finitely presented means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 0C5F (lemma-descend-nodal-family), combined with the absolute Noetherian approximation in the first paragraph of lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the geometric-fibre formulation is the equivalent nodal condition of lemma-nodal-family.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $S^\circ\ni s$ and then an affine open $X^\circ\ni x$ inside $f^{-1}(S^\circ)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The restricted morphism $h:X^\circ\to S^\circ$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Flatness and local finite presentation restrict by their local definitions [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The geometric fibres of $h$ are open subschemes of those of $f$, so they still have the stipulated completed local rings. They are empty or pure of dimension one: each component is a nonempty open of a component of the original fibre, whose dimension is unchanged by [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. Finally $x$ is nonsmooth for $h$, since smoothness of $h$ on a neighbourhood of $x$ would imply smoothness of $f$ there by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](b).

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, first paragraph: affine localisation on X and S.

proof.text: Write $S^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], it is the inverse limit of the spectra $S_i$ of finitely generated integer subalgebras of $A$, with affine transitions. The affine morphism $h$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). By [thm-pd-spreading-out](1), choose $a$ and a finitely presented $g_a:X_a\to S_a$ with $X^\circ\cong X_a\times_{S_a}S^\circ$. For $i\ge a$ put $X_i=X_a\times_{S_a}S_i$, $g_i:X_i\to S_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2)--(3) these maps remain finitely presented and $X_i$ is qcqs. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] their limit is $X^\circ$, also on directed tails. Each $X_i$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$: the union of generators for its finite-presentation chart algebra and for the base chart algebra generates their composite.

source.place: Tag 0CBY first proof first paragraph; Limits Tag 01ZM and Tag 01YZ for the models and their limit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-limit-lci-pure-stage] to $(g_i)$ and $h$. This gives $c\ge a$ such that every $g_i$ for $i\ge c$ is flat with pure-one-dimensional ordinary and geometric fibres, the latter local complete intersections.

source.place: Tag 0C5F (lemma-descend-nodal-family), first proof paragraph through relative-dimension descent; Tag 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci). Expanded using limits.tex Tags 0C3L (lemma-descend-syntomic) and 0EY2 (lemma-descend-dimension-d), and morphisms.tex Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], $\operatorname{Sing}(h)\to S^\circ$ is unramified. Apply [lem-trf-first-fitting-unramified-finite-stage] to $g_c$: for some $d\ge c$, $\operatorname{Sing}(g_d)\to S_d$ is unramified.

source.place: Tag 0C5F (lemma-descend-nodal-family), final proof paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 0C3I (lemma-base-change-and-fitting-ideal-omega); limits.tex Tag 0C4W (lemma-descend-unramified), whose local-finite-type hypotheses are verified here for the Fitting closed subscheme.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lci-unramified-singular-nodal-recognition] to $g_d$ using step 3 and step 4. Set $f_0=g_d$, $X_0=X_d$, $S_0=S_d$. Step 2 gives finite type over $\mathbf Z$, finite presentation, and the Cartesian identification (compose the two base changes by their universal properties). For the image $x_0$ of $x$, [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] identifies $\operatorname{Sing}(h)$ with the pullback of $\operatorname{Sing}(f_0)$, both with underlying nonsmooth loci. Since $x$ is nonsmooth for $h$, $x_0$ is nonsmooth for $f_0$.
